## Structural Criteria

<!-- Binary checks against the SKILL.md document itself. -->
<!-- Evaluated WITHOUT running the skill. -->

- [ ] **EVAL-S01:** Frontmatter complete (`name`, `description`, `domain`, `subdomain`, `scope`, `role`)
  - **Test:** Read SKILL.md frontmatter; verify all six required keys present and non-empty.
  - **Fail signal:** Any of the six keys is missing or has an empty value.

- [ ] **EVAL-S02:** `domain`, `subdomain`, `scope`, and `role` exist in `registry/SKILL_VOCABULARY.md`
  - **Test:** For each of the four values, verify a matching row exists in the corresponding section of `registry/SKILL_VOCABULARY.md`.
  - **Fail signal:** Any of the four slot values is absent from the vocabulary file.

- [ ] **EVAL-S03:** SKILL.md under 500 lines
  - **Test:** `wc -l SKILL.md` returns ≤ 500.
  - **Fail signal:** Line count exceeds 500.

- [ ] **EVAL-S04:** `Wrong-Tool Detection` section present and names sibling skills
  - **Test:** SKILL.md contains a `Wrong-Tool Detection` (or equivalent) section with at least one named redirect to another skill.
  - **Fail signal:** Section absent or contains only generic guidance without naming sibling skills.

- [ ] **EVAL-S05:** Every `Load:` path in SKILL.md resolves to an existing file
  - **Test:** Extract every `Load:` line; verify each referenced path exists on disk relative to the skill directory.
  - **Fail signal:** Any referenced load path does not exist.

- [ ] **EVAL-S06:** Skill listed in `registry/SKILL_REGISTRY.md` with `status` column populated
  - **Test:** Grep `registry/SKILL_REGISTRY.md` for the skill name; verify a row exists with a non-empty status value (draft / stable / deprecated).
  - **Fail signal:** No row found, or status column is empty.

- [ ] **EVAL-S07:** Domain README contains a row for this skill
  - **Test:** Verify `src/skills/delivery/README.md` includes a row linking the skill's SKILL.md path.
  - **Fail signal:** Row absent or links to a non-existent path.

- [ ] **EVAL-S08:** EVAL.md exists alongside SKILL.md (self-referential — passes by virtue of being written)
  - **Test:** Confirm `<skill-dir>/EVAL.md` is present.
  - **Fail signal:** EVAL.md absent (self-contradictory if this file exists).

## Execution Criteria

<!-- Binary checks against HOW the skill orchestrates execution. -->

- [ ] **EVAL-E01:** Sequential-default dispatch — only one subagent in flight at a time unless escape-hatch conditions are met
  - **Test:** Inspect the execution trace for Agent dispatches. Between any two adjacent dispatches, a completed closeout ingestion event ([INGEST-CLOSEOUT] completion) must appear. No two Agent calls are open concurrently unless the trace shows all three escape-hatch conditions were explicitly verified first (disjoint `touches`, zero `depends_on` coupling, in-session user authorization).
  - **Fail signal:** Two or more Agent calls are dispatched before the first one's closeout is ingested — no interleaved closeout parsing between dispatches.

- [ ] **EVAL-E02:** Resume detection short-circuits fresh-run phases
  - **Test:** When `.delivery/closeouts/` is non-empty at entry, the trace skips [INGEST-PLAN], [DECOMPOSE], and [CONFIRM] entirely and jumps directly to [PICK-NEXT-SLICE] after reconstructing slice statuses from the closeout trail.
  - **Fail signal:** [INGEST-PLAN] or [DECOMPOSE] executes when a non-empty closeout trail already exists — progress is silently re-decomposed.

- [ ] **EVAL-E03:** [CONFIRM] gate fires exactly once before the unattended loop begins, and is not auto-proceeded
  - **Test:** The trace shows the skill presenting INDEX.md to the user and pausing for explicit approval (Y or adjust) before dispatching any subagent. On an adjust response, INDEX.md is updated and re-presented before dispatch proceeds.
  - **Fail signal:** The first subagent dispatch occurs with no user-approval event in the trace between [DECOMPOSE] and [DISPATCH]; or [CONFIRM] is bypassed by treating an ambient "yes" as pre-authorization.

- [ ] **EVAL-E04:** [PRE-FLIGHT] hard checks run before any slice dispatch, with loud halt on failure
  - **Test:** The trace shows three explicit checks executed after [CONFIRM] and before [DISPATCH]: (1) `.delivery/` writability verified, (2) decomposed slice count ≥ 1 confirmed, (3) test framework discoverability confirmed via lockfile or config probe. If any check fails, the trace shows an error halt with a specific failure reason — no fallback or silent continuation.
  - **Fail signal:** A subagent is dispatched without all three pre-flight checks appearing in the trace; or a failed check is logged but execution continues into [DISPATCH].

- [ ] **EVAL-E05:** Each subagent prompt populates all 8 dispatch slots per `delivery-orchestration-dispatch-contract`
  - **Test:** Inspect each Agent dispatch prompt in the trace. All 8 required slots must appear: `slice_assignment`, `slice_id`, `attempt_number`, `dependency_closeouts` (distilled), `prior_attempt_closeouts`, `lessons_md`, `worker_protocols`, and `model`. The `worker_protocols` slot references `delivery-execution-slice-contract`, `delivery-execution-tdd-contract`, and `delivery-orchestration-closeout-schema` by name (not inlined).
  - **Fail signal:** Any of the 8 slots is absent from a dispatch prompt; or any protocol body is inlined into the prompt rather than referenced by name.

- [ ] **EVAL-E06:** Model is selected explicitly per slice — sonnet default, opus for architectural complexity
  - **Test:** Every Agent dispatch in the trace carries an explicit `model` parameter. Slices not flagged for architectural complexity use sonnet. Slices explicitly flagged for architectural complexity use opus. No dispatch inherits model by omission.
  - **Fail signal:** A dispatch prompt has no `model` parameter set; or a non-architectural slice is dispatched with opus; or a slice explicitly flagged for architectural complexity is dispatched with sonnet.

- [ ] **EVAL-E07:** [INGEST-CLOSEOUT] validates closeout schema before routing to [REPLAN]
  - **Test:** After each subagent completes, the trace shows YAML parse and field validation steps before [REPLAN] fires: required fields verified, `files_modified ⊆ slice.touches` checked, `pass ⇒ outcome_test_path populated and in tests_added` checked. On malformed YAML, a single retry with a parse-error hint is issued; a second malformation escalates rather than proceeding.
  - **Fail signal:** [REPLAN] fires immediately after closeout receipt with no validation trace between them; or a malformed closeout is accepted without a retry; or a second-malformation triggers a silent re-ingest instead of escalation.

- [ ] **EVAL-E08:** [REPLAN] is the sole writer to `.delivery/plan/` and `lessons.md` — subagent writes to those paths trigger halt-and-escalate
  - **Test:** Scan the trace for any file-write event targeting `.delivery/plan/`, `.delivery/lessons.md`, or slice frontmatter from within a subagent context (Agent thread). If any such write is detected, the trace must show a halt-and-escalate response from the main agent, not silent acceptance.
  - **Fail signal:** A write to `.delivery/plan/` or `lessons.md` from a subagent context is accepted without a halt event; or the main agent applies such a write without an escalation entry.

- [ ] **EVAL-E09:** Every plan/lessons mutation is logged in `.delivery/plan/CHANGELOG.md` in the same execution tick
  - **Test:** For each INDEX.md or `lessons.md` edit visible in the trace, a corresponding CHANGELOG.md entry appears within the same [REPLAN] phase — not deferred to a later tick or [TERMINATION].
  - **Fail signal:** A plan or lessons mutation appears in the trace with no CHANGELOG.md write in the same [REPLAN] block; or CHANGELOG.md is written in bulk at [TERMINATION] rather than per-mutation.

- [ ] **EVAL-E10:** Attempt-cap and replan-cap escalations trigger halt rather than continued dispatch
  - **Test:** When a slice reaches N=2 failed/blocked attempts, the trace shows the slice marked blocked and an escalation event — no further dispatch for that slice follows. When M=3 replan cycles accumulate on one slice, the trace shows a hard halt with the "plan likely fundamentally misframed" reason surfaced to the user.
  - **Fail signal:** A third dispatch attempt occurs for a slice after two non-passing closeouts; or a fourth replan cycle on one slice proceeds without a halt event.

- [ ] **EVAL-E11:** `delivery-plan-writer` stories are never re-decomposed — used as authoritative WP list by path-reference only
  - **Test:** When `.delivery/stories/TAG-NNN-*.md` story files + `STORIES.md` manifest are discovered at [INGEST-PLAN], the trace shows those files used as-is for INDEX.md construction (path references, not content copies). No [DECOMPOSE] step reframes or splits story boundaries.
  - **Fail signal:** A story's content is copied into `.delivery/plan/wp-<id>.md`; or [DECOMPOSE] rewrites or merges TAG-NNN boundaries when story files are present.

- [ ] **EVAL-E12:** [PICK-NEXT-SLICE] respects dependency order and does not dispatch slices with in-flight or failed dependencies
  - **Test:** Each dispatch is preceded by a visible dependency-eligibility check on the candidate slice. The selected slice's `depends_on` entries are all in a green/closed state before dispatch. If no slice is eligible because dependencies are blocked, the trace shows an escalation event rather than a dispatch.
  - **Fail signal:** A slice is dispatched while one of its `depends_on` entries is still in-flight, pending, or failed; or a blocked-dependency state causes silent stall rather than an escalation.

## Output Criteria

<!-- Binary checks against what the skill PRODUCES when run on a test prompt. -->

- [ ] **EVAL-O01:** Wrong-tool redirect is surfaced before any execution begins
  - **Test:** When the input matches a redirect condition (throughput-only dispatch, single-file improvement, plan decomposition without execution), verify the session emits a redirect to the named skill and stops — no `.delivery/` is created, no subagent is dispatched.
  - **Fail signal:** Execution proceeds (plan ingested, subagent dispatched, or `.delivery/` created) despite the input matching a redirect condition.

- [ ] **EVAL-O02:** Resume detection is performed and re-decomposition is skipped on resume
  - **Test:** When `.delivery/closeouts/` contains at least one file at session start, verify the output shows the skill skipping `[INGEST-PLAN]`/`[DECOMPOSE]`/`[CONFIRM]` and instead reconstructing slice status from the closeout trail before proceeding to `[PICK-NEXT-SLICE]`.
  - **Fail signal:** Session re-decomposes an existing plan, overwrites `INDEX.md`, or re-presents the WP approval gate on a resume.

- [ ] **EVAL-O03:** `[PRE-FLIGHT]` failures halt loudly with explicit failure identification
  - **Test:** Simulate each failing pre-flight condition in turn (no `.delivery/` writability, zero decomposable slices, no discoverable test framework) and verify the output names the specific failing check and stops without dispatching any subagent.
  - **Fail signal:** Execution continues past `[PRE-FLIGHT]` with a missing condition, or the halt message does not identify which check failed.

- [ ] **EVAL-O04:** Every subagent dispatch bundles all 8 required prompt slots
  - **Test:** Inspect each dispatch event in the transcript; verify the prompt includes `slice_assignment`, `slice_id`, `attempt_number`, `dependency_closeouts`, `prior_attempt_closeouts`, `lessons_md`, `worker_protocols`, and `model` — all 8 by name or explicit value, none omitted.
  - **Fail signal:** Any dispatch event is missing one or more of the 8 named slots.

- [ ] **EVAL-O05:** The three protocol references are injected into every subagent prompt by name, never inline
  - **Test:** For each dispatch, verify the prompt references `delivery-execution-slice-contract`, `delivery-execution-tdd-contract`, and `delivery-orchestration-closeout-schema` by name. Verify no prose or YAML body from any protocol appears verbatim in the dispatch prompt.
  - **Fail signal:** A protocol name is absent from a dispatch prompt, or the body of any protocol is reproduced inline.

- [ ] **EVAL-O06:** Model is selected explicitly per slice with correct default
  - **Test:** Verify every dispatch specifies a model explicitly. Verify `sonnet` is used unless the slice's frontmatter flags architectural complexity, in which case `opus` is used. No dispatch may omit the model field and rely on inheritance.
  - **Fail signal:** A dispatch occurs without an explicit model field, or `opus` is selected for a slice not flagged as architecturally complex.

- [ ] **EVAL-O07:** `CHANGELOG.md` entry is written in the same turn as every plan or lessons mutation
  - **Test:** For each turn where `INDEX.md`, any `wp-<id>.md`, or `lessons.md` is mutated, verify a corresponding entry in `.delivery/plan/CHANGELOG.md` is written in that same turn (not a later turn).
  - **Fail signal:** A plan or lessons file is edited in a turn that produces no `CHANGELOG.md` entry, or the `CHANGELOG.md` entry is written in a subsequent turn.

- [ ] **EVAL-O08:** Closeout validation enforces `files_modified ⊆ slice.touches` and rejects out-of-scope writes
  - **Test:** Inject a closeout where `files_modified` contains a path not in the slice's `touches` list; verify the session treats this as a contract violation (not a warning) and escalates rather than ingesting the closeout.
  - **Fail signal:** The session ingests a closeout whose `files_modified` includes a path outside `slice.touches`, or treats the violation as a warning and continues.

- [ ] **EVAL-O09:** Replan-cap and attempt-cap escalations fire at the defined thresholds and halt
  - **Test:** Verify that at N=2 failed/blocked attempts on one slice the slice is marked blocked and escalation occurs; verify that at M=3 replan cycles on one slice the session halts with the message "plan likely fundamentally misframed" and does not auto-dispatch a 4th attempt.
  - **Fail signal:** Dispatch continues past N=2 attempts without escalation, or a 4th replan cycle on one slice begins without halting.

- [ ] **EVAL-O10:** `delivery-plan-writer` TAG-NNN stories are used as-is and never re-decomposed
  - **Test:** When `.delivery/stories/TAG-NNN-*.md` story files + `STORIES.md` manifest are present, verify `INDEX.md` references those files by path and no new slice files are created by splitting or re-interpreting story content.
  - **Fail signal:** New `wp-<id>.md` files are materialized that duplicate or split TAG-NNN story content, or story bodies are copied into `.delivery/plan/`.

- [ ] **EVAL-O11:** The final summary conforms to the required verbatim shape from `final-summary-format.md`
  - **Test:** At `[TERMINATION]`, verify the output contains all required sections in order: `## Run summary` header with ISO date and plan-source pointer; `**Exit reason:**` with exactly one value from the four-value enum; `### Slice rollup` table with status rows summing to `total`; `### Slice detail` table with a row for every slice including undispatched ones; `### Lessons tail` with 5–10 verbatim lesson strings (if `lessons.md` is non-empty); `### Pointers` with all four static paths; `### Next move` with exactly one sentence.
  - **Fail signal:** Any required section is absent, the rollup counts do not sum to `total`, the slice detail table omits any slice, lessons are paraphrased rather than quoted, pointers are missing, or `Next move` contains multiple sentences or proposes an auto-rerun.

- [ ] **EVAL-O12:** Exit reason is drawn from the four-value enum and not invented
  - **Test:** Verify the `Exit reason` field in every final summary contains exactly one of: `all_slices_green`, `escalated_blocked`, `escalated_replan_cap`, `user_interrupt` — no other values are accepted.
  - **Fail signal:** The exit reason field contains a value not in the enum, is absent, or lists more than one value.

- [ ] **EVAL-O13:** Sequential dispatch invariant holds — no concurrent subagents unless all three escape-hatch conditions are met and user has explicitly authorized parallel
  - **Test:** Inspect the transcript for any turn where two subagents are dispatched. For each such turn, verify all three conditions are satisfied: (1) the two slices' `touches` sets are provably disjoint, (2) neither slice `depends_on` the other directly or transitively, (3) the session transcript shows in-session user authorization by name before the parallel dispatch occurs.
  - **Fail signal:** Two subagents are dispatched in the same turn without all three conditions being met, or parallel dispatch occurs without explicit in-session user authorization.

- [ ] **EVAL-O14:** Subagents are prevented from writing to plan, lessons, or slice frontmatter — violation triggers halt and escalation
  - **Test:** Inject a subagent closeout that claims to have written to `.delivery/plan/` or `.delivery/lessons.md`; verify the session halts and escalates rather than ingesting or ignoring the write.
  - **Fail signal:** The session ingests a closeout reporting writes to protected paths without halting, or the violation is logged as a warning and the loop continues.

- [ ] **EVAL-O15:** Confirmation gate is presented exactly once and loop does not auto-proceed
  - **Test:** On a fresh run, verify the session presents `INDEX.md` to the user and waits for explicit approval (`Y` or an adjustment) before entering `[PRE-FLIGHT]`. Verify no subagent is dispatched before approval is recorded.
  - **Fail signal:** The loop enters `[PRE-FLIGHT]` or dispatches a subagent without a recorded user approval, or the confirmation gate is presented more than once after an approved WP list.

## Test Prompts

<!-- Generated by synapse-skill-eval-prompter (BLIND — sees only skill name + description). -->

### Naive User

1. "ok i think we're ready, go ahead and build it"
   - *Tests whether the skill determines if a deliverable plan exists and how it handles a start signal with zero context provided.*

2. "can you ship the auth stuff we talked about? just start building"
   - *Tests whether the skill recovers a plan from prior conversation or recognizes missing structured input and handles it gracefully.*

3. "execute the plan for the dashboard and also the notifications, whatever we decided"
   - *Exercises how the skill handles a vague multi-slice signal where the plan itself is assumed but never stated.*

### Experienced User

4. "We have a four-slice delivery plan: slice-1 (DB schema migrations), slice-2 (repository layer over those tables), slice-3 (REST endpoints consuming the repo), slice-4 (integration tests against the endpoints). Slices 2-4 are sequentially gated on the prior slice passing CI. Execute end-to-end. Halt and surface blockers if any slice fails its gate."
   - *Stresses dependency-chain awareness, gate enforcement between slices, and correct ordering — not just parallel dispatch.*

5. "/build — we have three parallel slices: billing-webhook-handler, subscription-state-machine, and invoice-pdf-generator. All three write to the same `ledger_events` table. Coordinate so their migrations don't conflict, then run the slices concurrently once the schema is stable. Flag any merge risk before execution starts."
   - *Tests whether the skill detects cross-slice shared state risks before dispatching concurrently, rather than blindly firing all slices at once.*

6. "We ran /build last Tuesday. Slices 1 and 2 completed. Slice 3 failed on the payments service timeout bug we since fixed. Slice 4 was never started. Resume from slice 3, skip re-running 1 and 2, and carry through to completion."
   - *Tests mid-plan resumption — whether the skill can pick up a partially executed plan without re-executing already-completed slices.*

### Adversarial

7. "ship this — auth, payments, data pipeline, admin portal, notification system, mobile API, and the analytics backend. all of it. one go."
   - *A seven-domain all-at-once execution request that should trigger a scoping challenge or decomposition gate, not blind acceptance.*

8. "execute the plan but run all slices in parallel and also make sure each slice is gated on the previous one passing before it starts. do both."
   - *Directly contradictory instructions (fully parallel vs. fully sequential gating) — the skill must detect the conflict and surface it rather than silently pick one.*

### Wrong Tool

9. "write the repository layer for the user profile service — just the CRUD methods against the postgres table"
   - *A single-task implementation request with no plan to orchestrate — sounds adjacent but belongs to a direct implementation skill.*

10. "we need to deliver the reporting module — can you figure out how to break it into slices and sequence the work before we start building?"
    - *The user wants a delivery plan authored, not an existing plan executed — a near-miss that belongs to a planning or scoping skill rather than this executor.*
